title: ‘A = 440 Hz’ is a 20th-century agreement, not a law of nature
body: Across European history, the A above middle C has been tuned anywhere from roughly 400 to over 460 Hz, depending on city, era and instrument. An international conference in London settled on 440 Hz in 1939, and the standard was later adopted by ISO. Even now many orchestras tune a little higher, around 442 Hz, for a brighter sound, while baroque ensembles often play at about 415 Hz.
